## Findings
- claim-1: The requested bounded full-text excerpt cannot be retrieved: `source-29` is not a citable indexed file, and no supplied FULL-TEXT SOURCE block contains equations (8)–(10), Definition 2.1, Lemma 2.5, or Theorems 4.4–4.5.
- claim-2: The external search identifies St. Dizier–Yong’s 2024 paper and its abstract says “We prove the minimality conjecture,” but this is metadata/abstract material, not a theorem-level locator. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
- claim-3: The supplied local source is instead the 2011 Reiner–Woo–Yong paper, identified as arXiv:0809.2981v2. [source-5@L11-L22|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-4: The requested target is **not established**: no uncorrupted bounded source-29 excerpt was available, so theorem hypotheses cannot be distinguished rigorously from proof-only restrictions.
## Strategy
Use the recorded alternate-provider searches (arXiv, Semantic Scholar, Crossref). Treat DOI metadata, abstract material, and the 2011 paper only as identification evidence, not substitutes for source-29’s requested text.

## Gaps
No retrieved citable full-text passage contains equations (8)–(10), complete Definition 2.1, Lemma 2.5, Theorems 4.4–4.5, and their linkage. Alternate providers were queried but returned no such full text in this bounded search. Thus theorem hypotheses cannot be distinguished from proof-local restrictions.

The requested target is **not established from the supplied evidence**.

## Next
Obtain one hashed bounded full-text excerpt for source-29 from an alternate provider, with stable locators covering all specified items; then classify each restriction from the cited text.
